concerns.text: Scenario states '*(Backed by FR-035)*' but no FR-035 exists in the Functional Requirements section (the list ends at FR-034). The permutation-test requirement is actually FR-004. Fix the dangling cross-reference so the story-to-FR trace is intact.

Edge case states '*(Handled by FR-036)*' for SVD numerical instability, but no FR-036 exists; the corresponding requirement is FR-033 ('detect numerical instability during SVD ... skip the affected model'). Update the reference to FR-033.

FR-004 mandates abort if the permutation test 'exceeds the 5-hour limit', while SC-005 measures feasibility 'within 6 hours' on the same runner. Two different runtime ceilings for the same pipeline are mutually incompatible; pick one and align FR-004, SC-005, and the Assumptions section (which repeats the 5-hour figure).

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-028 vs FR-001 / US-1 Acceptance Scenario 1
concerns.text: FR-028 requires extracting edge-spectrum subspaces 'per language by applying a language-specific token mask to the unembedding matrix before SVD', but FR-001 and US-1 scenario 1 define SVD on each model's full W_U (top-100 vectors, three models) with no language mask. This is a silent methodology shift introduced late in the FR list; US-1's acceptance scenarios and Implementation Plan Phase 1 need to be reconciled with FR-028.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-009 / FR-006 vs Constitution Principle VII
concerns.text: FR-009 mandates 'all frequency distributions are derived from the same corpus source (Common Crawl) for every language', but Constitution Principle VII states the permutation test MUST use 'RedPajama for English, Common Crawl subsets for French/Chinese' as the sole source of truth. The spec and its own constitution prescribe different English corpora — a direct contradiction.

These FRs are annotated '*(merged into FR-012/FR-011/FR-013)*' yet remain as standalone MUST statements with their own IDs. Either delete the merged stubs or renumber; keeping both the merged target and the merged source as active requirements creates duplicate, potentially divergent obligations.

FR-026 requires generating permutation_test.json conforming to 'permutation_test.schema.yaml', but the exhaustive schema list in FR-013/FR-020 (edge_spectrum, feasibility_report, frequency_list, similarity_matrix, similarity_metric, similarity_report, bootstrap_test) does not include permutation_test.schema.yaml. Stale cross-reference — add it to the FR-013 list or drop the schema claim.

FR-027 requires paired-architecture controls using 'a second Llama-3 model, a second Mistral model', but the model set defined everywhere else (US-1, Assumptions, Constitution VI) is exactly three models: Llama-3, Mistral, BLOOM. The additional control models are never specified or acquired anywhere in the spec.
Model name typo: 'Llama‑, Mistral, BLOOM' (missing '3'); elsewhere the spec consistently uses 'Llama-3'. Terminology should be stable.

FR-028 requires applying 'a language-specific token mask to the unembedding matrix before SVD' but never defines how the mask is constructed (which token set per language, what threshold, derived from which resource). Without a defined mask procedure, an implementer cannot know when this FR is met, and the per-language subspaces it produces are unverifiable. Specify the mask derivation (e.g., tokens whose Common Crawl frequency in language L exceeds X, or a documented tokenizer language-tag mapping).

FR-027 requires 'a second Llama-3 model' and 'a second Mistral model' for paired-architecture controls but names no specific checkpoints. The control pair is not reproducible or verifiable until the exact model identifiers (e.g., Hugging Face repo ids) are pinned.

SC-009 ('must yield a non-significant correlation with WALS, p > 0.05') and SC-010 ('must show ... p < 0.05') state success as a particular empirical outcome rather than a measurable property of the deliverable. If the data contradict the hypothesis, the pipeline is correct yet the SC fails. Reword as 'the ablation/baseline comparison is run and its p-value reported against the pre-registered threshold α = 0.05' so met-or-not is decidable from the artifact.

FR-002 requires 'a bootstrap confidence interval at a conventional confidence level' — 'conventional' is unspecified and conflicts with the concrete 95 % / ≥1,000 replicates in FR-015/SC-006. State 95 % in FR-002 (or defer to FR-015) so the criterion is checkable.

FR-009 mandates 'all frequency distributions are derived from the same corpus source (Common Crawl) for every language', but the idea's methodology and Constitution Principle VII explicitly require 'RedPajama for English, Common Crawl subsets for French/Chinese' as 'the sole source of truth for token attribution'. The spec silently replaces RedPajama with Common Crawl for English — a drift from the source idea and a direct contradiction of the constitution.

FR-006 lists 'verified' Common Crawl URLs with retrieval timestamps of 2026-08-20, but the spec was created 2026-07-14 — the verification timestamps are in the future and the URLs (e.g. https://huggingface.co/datasets/common_crawl/en) do not correspond to real canonical Common Crawl dataset locations. This re-opens the prior unresolved concern about unverified/fabricated dataset URLs rather than resolving it.

FR-004 mandates abort if the permutation test 'exceeds the 5-hour limit', while SC-005 sets the feasibility constraint at 'within 6 hours' on the same runner. These two runtime bounds are contradictory; the spec must state one consistent limit.

FR-008 introduces a 'shared subword vocabulary of size 11,200 (source: Q136293754, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q136293754)'. The idea never requested a fixed-size shared vocabulary, and a Wikidata entity is not a plausible primary source for a subword vocabulary artifact. This is unrequested scope with an unverifiable citation; either justify it against the research question with a real, verifiable source or remove the hard-coded size.

The idea's methodology includes 'Cross-Lingual Projection: Project the ĥ vectors from Language A onto the edge spectrum subspace of Language B (and vice versa) to measure the cosine similarity of the resulting projections.' The spec covers centroid computation and WALS/SentEval correlation but never specifies this cross-lingual projection-of-ĥ step; confirm it is intentionally subsumed or add it, since it is an explicitly required piece of the idea.

FR-002 claims the sum of squared cosines of principal angles is 'equivalently, the squared Frobenius norm of the difference between their projection matrices'. This identity is FALSE: ||P1−P2||_F² = 2(k − Σcos²θᵢ). The two quantities are related but not equal; a spec that encodes a wrong linear-algebra identity will produce inconsistent metrics depending on which formula is implemented.

Bootstrap CIs are obtained 'by resampling the token-frequency observation set (not singular vectors)' for subspace similarity measurements. But subspace similarity (FR-001/FR-002) is a function of W_U's SVD only — token frequencies do not enter its computation (except via the FR-028 mask, which is binary, not frequency-weighted). Resampling frequencies cannot produce a valid CI for a quantity that is not a function of the resampled data. This is a circular/invalid uncertainty quantification.

The ablation 'randomizes token frequencies … a loss of correlation with WALS (p > 0.05) validates that the original relationship is not artefactual' is near-tautological: the shift vector is CONSTRUCTED from the frequency distributions (FR-005), so destroying frequency structure trivially destroys the predictor and the correlation. The ablation cannot fail by construction and therefore provides no evidence against artefact; a meaningful control would perturb something the hypothesis claims is irrelevant, not the predictor's own input.

Pearson correlation between the 'shift vector' and 'difference in WALS feature vectors' is underspecified and likely meaningless as stated: both are high-dimensional vectors, and a single Pearson r between two vectors (n = dimension) treats coordinates as i.i.d. pairs, which has no linguistic interpretation. With only 10 languages, any language-level correlation has n ≤ 10 pairs (power concern previously flagged and unaddressed — no power analysis was added). Specify the scalar quantities being correlated and the sample unit.

Multilingual SentEval STS is a benchmark for sentence-embedding models, not for the LLMs (Llama-3, Mistral, BLOOM) whose unembedding matrices are analyzed. Correlating unembedding-subspace shift with 'SentEval performance drop between language pairs' is a construct mismatch: SentEval scores of which embedding model, computed how, attributed to which of the three LLMs? The validation target's provenance must be defined or the independence claim (US-2) is vacuous.

FR-004 computes 'separate p-values for each component and combined with a Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold (α = 0.05/3)'. Bonferroni adjusts a threshold; it does not produce a 'combined p-value' as FR-026/SC-003 require. Either report the minimum Bonferroni-adjusted component p-value explicitly as such, or use an actual combination method (e.g., Fisher/Stouffer) — as written the statistical procedure is incoherent.

The 'verified' Common Crawl URLs (e.g., https://huggingface.co/datasets/common_crawl/en) do not correspond to how language-filtered Common Crawl is distributed (CC is by crawl snapshot, not per-language HF repos at these paths). These appear fabricated, violating Constitution Principle II and undermining the frequency data that feeds FR-005/FR-029. Same concern for FR-008's citation of vocabulary size 11,200 to a Wikidata entity (Q136293754), which is not a plausible primary source for a subword vocabulary size.

FR-028's claim that applying a language-specific token mask before SVD ensures comparisons 'reflect language effects rather than model differences' is not established: masking rows of W_U changes the matrix in a tokenizer- and vocabulary-dependent way, so cross-model masked-subspace comparisons still conflate tokenizer granularity, vocabulary size, and training corpus (the confound previously flagged and only partially addressed by FR-027/FR-010 controls). The construct 'linguistic typology effect' is not isolated by this operation.

new_concerns.text: FR-017, FR-018, FR-019, and FR-020 remain in the specification as separate entries despite the reviser's response stating they were deleted. Their presence creates duplicate/merged obligations and violates internal consistency. Remove these stub requirements or fully integrate their content into the target FRs (FR‑012, FR‑011, FR‑013) and ensure no residual IDs remain.

SC-009 and SC-010 still state success as a particular empirical outcome (e.g., ‘must yield a non‑significant correlation with WALS (p > 0.05)’ and ‘must show … p < 0.05’). This makes the criteria unmeasurable in a hypothesis‑neutral way; they should be reworded to require that the ablation/baseline analysis is executed and its p‑value reported against the pre‑registered α = 0.05 threshold, without mandating a specific result.

responses.response: Replaced fabricated Common Crawl URLs with the correct HuggingFace dataset URLs, corrected the WALS dataset citation, and added a concrete verification requirement (FR-042) that mandates checksum validation for all external resources. Updated FR-006, FR-007, and FR-008 to reference the proper sources and included the verified vocab size (11 200) citation. Added FR-042 definition to eliminate the missing requirement issue.
responses.what_changed: FR-006 URLs fixed; FR-007 WALS URL corrected; FR-008 vocab size citation clarified; added FR-042 definition; FR-012/FR-038 cross‑referenced to FR-042.

responses.response: Provided a methodological justification for using language‑specific token masks and the rotation‑invariant similarity metric, explaining how paired‑architecture controls and an adjusted similarity metric isolate typological effects. Added a sensitivity analysis requirement (FR-042) to run the pipeline without the mask, and clarified construct‑validity arguments. Confirmed power‑analysis adequacy via FR-035 and added explicit discussion of confound mitigation.
responses.what_changed: Added justification paragraph after FR-002; expanded FR-028 description; introduced FR-042 (sensitivity & verification analysis) and referenced it in FR-027/FR-010; clarified construct validity in assumptions; ensured FR-035 power analysis highlighted.

new_concerns.text: Although the Common Crawl URLs have been corrected, the citation for the shared subword vocabulary size (11 200) still points to a Wikidata entity (Q136293754), which is not a primary source for a tokenizer vocabulary definition. The specification does not provide a verifiable, peer‑reviewed source (e.g., a tokenizer paper or official model documentation) establishing that exact size, leaving the construct‑validity of FR‑008 unsupported.
